entry: Ran lifecycle/session-switch.mjs (createSessionSwitching) with scripted manager, route/cwd setters, status routes, agent tool, memory ingest and surface closer, and a scripted forgetSessionSearch (mock.module); deleted rows are real <id>.json files in a scratch MIXDOG_DATA_DIR sessions dir. Did not run the real manager, store or worktree cleanup (cleanupDeletedSessionWorktree is a scripted endpoint recording its arguments).
exclusions: a function in a recorded call argument (the close option isSessionLive) cannot be encoded: it is recorded as {function: name, resultAtCall, resultAfterOp}, its own return value at the call and after the op
the scratch data dir path is replaced by <DATA> in the one value that holds it: the result of sessionStoreDir() (case 255); the separator is the one Node produced
the store dir is emptied and rewritten with the case's rows before every case (as in the test); its listing is recorded in the OS order, unsorted

state (session, route, desktop, cwd) is not compared: it is Node's single runtime's current-session state; the daemon holds threads a client names, and a thread's cwd and route are its own (decisions.md, "wp-run-host: thread/switchContext retargets no global")

the calls that retarget Node's runtime for its next session are not compared: clearPrep, cwd, setRoute, refreshEffort in switchContext (decisions.md, same entry), and the whole call list of a delete of the current session (line 116 run 2, line 198: release, tombstoning close, cwd, invalidations, create of the replacement), which the core does not have: its delete of the thread a client has open is the same thread/delete, and the replacement is the client's next thread/start

cleaned: only each call's deleted session id is compared; the core's worktree cleanup (DeleteSeams::release_deleted_worktree -> worktree_maintenance.rs cleanup_deleted_session) takes the session id alone, Node's scripted endpoint also records the runtime's current session and cwd at the call
listed (line 159): only each row's id is compared; Node's lead-catalog row fields are listSessions' own projection, the core's thread/list answers its ThreadSummary rows
storeFiles (line 152): Node's store dir holds <id>.json per session; the core's store holds a folder per session, so the stored sessions are compared as <id>.json

result of newSession (line 244): the id thread/start mints is compared as the recorded "fresh" when it is a new thread (not the one open); its calls (cli-new close of the open conversation, ingest, invalidateContext, create) are not compared: thread/start leaves the threads a client holds open

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: mixdog-core-session, over the real thread store in a scratch data dir (session/switch_replay.rs): deleteSession -> thread/delete (directory.rs -> delete.rs delete_session), switchContext -> SessionContextSwitch::switch_context (thread_switches.rs, the ContextSwitch ThreadSettings serves thread/switchContext with), newSession -> thread/start, listSessions -> thread/list (ThreadListService over the store's index), prefetchSession -> the thread's open, sessionStoreDir -> the store's sessions folder (StoreThreads::over_data_dir). The recorded rows are threads created under their ids (create_with_id) with their header fields, their messages a turn. The calls are read off the core: the delete's fence of the thread (close), DeleteSeams::release_session_work (cancelTasks then clearRoute, purge.rs release_session_work), the delete mark (delete), the close-time memory ingest (ingest), the context target's invalidations (invalidateContext, invalidateTools); cleaned and forgotten are the DeleteSeams releaseDeletedWorktree and forgetSessionSearch calls.
